messages:
jamal: quick sync — we have a flaky streaming client that reauths via cross-org impersonation (workload-identity -> OIDC -> target SA) and on reconnect we get a 401 about audience. happens ~50% of reconnects :grimacing:
alex: can you paste the minimal logs? is it 401 from the server or from the token exchange step?
maria: :thinking: audience mismatch usually means the token given to the server has aud != the endpoint expected (or the server expects an internal audience). are you exchanging to the right target_audience or using token type JWT vs access token?
jamal: server 401 during GRPC handshake. logs from client: 
```
WARN reconnect: bidi_stream failed: rpc error: code = Unauthenticated desc = token audience mismatch
DEBUG token-exchange: got token (aud="https://redwood.api.prod") ttl=59s
```
we appear to be getting a short-lived token with aud set to the redwood API url, but the server wants the project-scoped audience (projects/12345/locations/...). only fails when the stream has been open >30s and then reconnects (so reauth path triggered).
kevin: likely candidate: your intermediate OIDC exchange is returning an access token with the OIDC client_id as aud, but the impersonation step needs the service-account impersonation to specify `audience` (or for access tokens you set `scope`). in short: token you present to grpc!=token server expects.
sarah: language-specific gotcha: a lot of SDK token sources cache a Token object and reuse it until expiry. if your server validates aud at stream start but your reconnect code reuses cached token from the wrong issuer/aud, you hit 401. verify your Reauth path refreshes the TokenSource before dialing.
jamal: we are using Python client with google-auth style impersonation + custom OIDC exchange. config snippet: 
```
# pseudo
oidc_resp = requests.post(wip_pool_url, data={...})
impersonated = iam.credentials.generate_access_token(name=target_sa, delegates=[], scope=["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"])
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {impersonated['accessToken']}"}
# then grpc channel created with those headers
```
we thought impersonated token would be valid for stream reconnects but looks like the OIDC-issued token is ephemeral and we don't always re-run the chain on reconnect.
maria: in python make sure your channel credentials are built with a callback that reads current token per-RPC, not a one-time header. e.g. pass a metadata plugin that calls the token source on every call. otherwise initial dial works but reconnect reuses stale header.
kevin: for Go folks: avoid using oauth2.ReuseTokenSource with a single static provider in long-lived streams. use oauth2.Transport with a TokenSource that always fetches from impersonation client (or wrap with a tiny mutex-refresh so you never hand out expired aud).
jamal: tested a fix: switched to per-request metadata callback that calls impersonation API again on reconnect. seems much better but still saw ~5% fails. stack traces show sometimes the impersonation API returns a token with aud set to the original workload-identity pool client_id (not the service account).
sarah: that's a bug in the exchange order: you should first exchange OIDC -> impersonation (generateAccessToken) and then present that token. If you accidentally present raw OIDC token to the grpc endpoint, aud will differ. Also check your impersonation call's `includeEmail`/`delegates` args — some flows change the returned token shape.
alex: another trick: if your control plane supports stable audiences, mint tokens with a slightly longer TTL and validate refresh jitter. also add a tiny jitter before reconnect to avoid thundering token refreshes that hit IAM rate limits.
jamal: added jitter + per-request metadata plugin + a sanity check that aud contains "projects/12345". after 24h load test, reconnect error rate dropped to 0.2%. thanks everyone.
maria: nice. can you open a short PR in sdk-auth with the metadata-plugin example (python + go) so others can copy? label as "auth: streaming reconnect".
jamal: yes will do. PR will include a minimal python metadata plugin snippet and go TokenSource wrapper.
dev-bot: deploy:ci jamal/streaming-auth-fix queued — tests passing. :rocket:
